subject: Prescription Pearls
title: Antibiotic Stewardship: Empirical Choices
preview: Empirical antimicrobial decisions balance immediate infection risk with local susceptibility and safe de-escalation.

sections.title: Initial selection
points: A rapidly deteriorating patient may require urgent empiric treatment after appropriate cultures, without dangerous delay.
Drug choice varies by syndrome, local resistance, patient factors and infection-control setting.

sections.title: Review and stewardship
points: Ensure source control when needed and check the adequacy of route, penetration and targeted coverage.
Review therapy when microbiology and the clinical course clarify the diagnosis; duration is syndrome-specific.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: The newest or broadest antibiotic is not universally the best treatment.
An arbitrary fixed duration cannot replace source control, response and guideline context.

quickRevision: Start by identifying the likely site of infection, severity, host factors and likely pathogens.
Check allergy, renal or hepatic impairment, prior antibiotic exposure and local resistance data.
Reassess cultures and response promptly; narrow or stop unnecessary therapy when clinically appropriate.

quiz.question: What should influence empirical antimicrobial selection?
options: Likely site, local resistance, severity and allergy
quiz.explanation: Empirical antibiotics should cover the likely pathogens while considering illness severity, allergy history, renal function and local resistance patterns; reassess once microbiology results return.
